report.source_text: In addition to the tumor itself, a sample of the fluid from the cyst and peritoneal washing was sent to the department of pathology for examination. Both were fixated with 10% neutral buffered formalin and preserved from clotting with heparin. No malignant cells were found in either of them. In peritoneal washing, mesothelial cells, inflammatory cells and numerous erythrocytes were reported.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old woman presented with significant abdominal enlargement, left-sided abdominal pain, menstrual irregularity, and infertility. Pelvic ultrasound revealed a massive fluid-filled tumor with segmental solid components, though the precise origin was obscured by the tumor size and patient obesity. Serum tumor markers (CA-125, HE4, CEA, AFP, and others) were within normal ranges, arguing against malignancy. Surgical exploration with tumor resection was performed. Histopathological examination of the tumor confirmed the diagnosis of serous cystadenofibroma of the ovary. Peritoneal washing and cyst fluid showed no malignant cells, supporting a benign diagnosis. Admission physical exam showed the patient was afebrile with mildly elevated vital signs but was otherwise in moderate condition.
